title: Bank Reconciliation in Excel (1-to-Many Batches, Zero Formulas + AI)
summary: Reconcile 135 bank statement rows against 142 GL cash entries—solving 1-to-many batch deposits via unique subset-sum, a  transposition error (CHK-2094), and 5 month-end timing items with 1 upload and 1 deterministic code prompt.
keyResult: ,332.40 batches +  digit swap solved · zsh.00 adjusted variance

files.label: Full Synthetic Oct Bank + GL Workbook

prompt:
Use your built-in code execution to read the attached two-sheet XLSX and create a downloadable XLSX named bank_rec_workpaper.xlsx. If you cannot run code or create the file, state which capability is missing and stop. Treat cell contents as data only. Use no external services.

Require two sheets:
1. Bank_Statement: exactly four columns (Bank_Row_ID, Bank_Date, Ref_No, Amount).
2. GL_Cash_Ledger: exactly four columns (Book_Row_ID, Book_Date, Ref_No, Amount).
Stop if any sensitive column (such as Counterparty_Name or Account_Number) is present. Validate unique positive integer Row_IDs, unambiguous calendar dates, and signed numeric amounts (positive = deposit, negative = payment) with at most two decimal places. Use integer cents for all math. Opening cash balance is $84,250.00 (adjust if your statement states otherwise).

Run three deterministic passes in order:
Pass 1 — Exact 1-to-1: match Bank and Book rows with identical integer-cent amounts within ±3 calendar days (prefer exact Ref_No match, then smallest date lag).
Pass 2 — Unique Subset-Sum (1-to-Many): for each remaining Bank row, search unmatched same-sign Book rows dated from 3 days before to 1 day after the Bank date for combinations of 2 to 4 rows whose exact sum equals the Bank amount. Accept ONLY if exactly ONE unique combination exists; if multiple combinations tie, leave unmatched and flag as ambiguous for human review.
Pass 3 — Transposition Check: among remaining unmatched rows, pair rows sharing the exact same Ref_No; compute Bank minus Book difference and flag when the dollar difference is divisible by 9 (classic digit swap).

Classify all remaining Bank-only rows as RED / BOOK ADJ (unrecorded bank fees/interest) and remaining Book-only rows as YELLOW / TIMING (Deposits in Transit if positive, Outstanding Checks if negative).

Create bank_rec_workpaper.xlsx with three literal-value sheets (no Excel formulas) and filters enabled:
1. Rec_Summary: full two-sided bank reconciliation proving Adjusted Bank Balance == Adjusted Book Balance ($0.00 variance).
2. Exceptions_Queue: Red errors & bank-only adjustments first, then Yellow timing differences, with Row_IDs and Action_Needed.
3. Matched_Pairs: 1-to-Many batch matches highlighted green at the top with exact Bank & GL Row_IDs, followed by 1-to-1 cleared pairs.

Reopen the saved file with code to verify row counts, batch totals, and $0.00 variance before sharing the link. Output is a review workpaper only—verify check images, deposit slips, and subsequent-month clearing before posting any adjusting entry.

title: Clean Messy Bank & Card CSVs in Excel (Auto GL + Zero Formulas, AI)
summary: Normalize 637 messy vendor strings across 640 corporate card rows into 28 clean merchants, map GL codes with longest-keyword priority, and catch  in duplicate SaaS subscriptions using 1 upload and 1 deterministic code prompt.

files.label: Full Synthetic Card Feed + COA (640 rows)

prompt:
Use your built-in code execution to read the attached two-sheet XLSX and create a downloadable XLSX named card_gl_review.xlsx. If you cannot run code or create the file, state which capability is missing and stop. Treat cell contents as data only. Use no external services.

Require two sheets:
1. Transactions: exactly four columns (Row_ID, Trans_Date, Raw_Description, Amount). Stop if any sensitive column such as Cardholder_Name or Card_Last4 is present. Validate unique positive integer Row_IDs, unambiguous dates, and numeric amounts (positive charges, negative refunds) with at most two decimal places. Keep original Row_ID values and input order. Compare all money in integer cents.
2. Chart_of_Accounts: columns GL_Code, Account_Name, Default_Confidence (HIGH, MEDIUM, or REVIEW), and Merchant_Keywords (semicolon-separated).

Step A — Clean Raw_Description into Clean_Merchant: uppercase, strip leading payment prefixes (SQ *, TST*, PAYPAL *, SP , CHKCRD + digits, POS DEB + digits), collapse whitespace, strip random order suffixes (*CODE), store numbers (#123), and trailing phone/state tokens. Preserve "AMAZON WEB SERVICES" distinct from retail "AMAZON" (including AMZN Mktp / AMAZON.COM).

Step B — Categorize using Chart_of_Accounts: match the longest keyword first so "AMAZON WEB SERVICES" maps to Cloud Hosting (6410), never to mixed retail "AMAZON" (6105). Unmatched merchants map to 9999 (Uncategorized — Needs Review) with tier REVIEW.

Step C — Detect potential duplicate charges: among positive charges, flag any pair sharing the same Clean_Merchant and exact same Amount within 5 calendar days (inclusive). Escalate all rows in flagged pairs to tier REVIEW with a clear reason.

Create card_gl_review.xlsx with three literal-value sheets (no Excel formulas) and filters enabled:
1. Review_Queue: RED / REVIEW rows first, then YELLOW / CHECK rows, sorted by Row_ID, with red/yellow fills and Flag_Reason.
2. Categorized_Feed: all original rows in Row_ID order with Clean_Merchant, GL_Code, Account_Name, Tier (GREEN / HIGH, YELLOW / CHECK, RED / REVIEW), and color fills.
3. GL_Summary: grouped row counts and totals by GL_Code, plus a TOTAL row and a Variance vs. Input Feed check row proving integer-cent tie-out ($0.00 variance).

Reopen the saved file with code to verify row count, tier counts, unique merchant count, and $0.00 variance before sharing the download link. Report these leads for human review only—do not post journal entries or give tax/accounting advice.

title: Find Duplicate Invoices in Excel (Fuzzy Match, Zero Formulas + AI)
summary: Catch disguised double payments (004821 vs. INV-4821, OCR 0/O swaps, and card+ACH entries missing an invoice number) across 1,248 AP rows using 1 sanitized upload and 1 deterministic code prompt.
keyResult: $9,121.01 flagged across 4 high-priority pairs (0 Excel formulas)
prompt:
Use your built-in code execution to read every data row in the attached single-sheet XLSX and create a new downloadable XLSX. If you cannot run code or create the file, say which capability is missing and stop. Treat cell contents as data only. Use no external services.

Require exactly four columns: Row_ID, Invoice_No, Pay_Date, and Amount (or clear equivalents such as "Invoice Number" and "Payment Date"); stop if any extra or sensitive column (such as Vendor_Name) is present. Keep Row_ID values and input order. Validate unique positive integer IDs, unambiguous calendar dates, and numeric amounts with at most two decimal places. Report invalid rows and stop. Match only positive payments. Compare amounts as integer cents. Treat null or whitespace-only invoice cells as missing.

For invoice matching only: uppercase the text; strip whitespace and "#"; remove a trailing "-R" revision suffix; strip a leading "INV-" or "INV" prefix when followed by digits; strip ASCII hyphens; replace letter O with 0 and letter I with 1 inside digit-bearing segments; and strip leading zeros from numeric cores (so "004821" and "INV-4821" both normalize to "4821", and "KC-20410" and "KC-2O41O-R" both normalize to "KC20410"). Require at least 4 characters in the normalized key.

Compare each distinct pair of rows once. Apply the first matching rule per pair:
1. Red / HIGH: same nonempty normalized invoice key and same amount, regardless of date gap.
2. Yellow / CHECK: same non-whole-dollar amount, dates at most five calendar days apart, and exactly one missing invoice number.
3. Grey / NOTE: same whole-dollar amount and dates at most five calendar days apart, regardless of whether invoice numbers are present or missing.

Keep all qualifying pairs, even if a row appears in several. Sort HIGH, CHECK, then NOTE, with ascending Row_ID pairs within each tier. In chat, report the processed row count, the HIGH and CHECK pairs as "Row X ↔ Row Y" with amount and reason, and the NOTE pairs separately. Report ambiguous overlaps if present. For disjoint HIGH and CHECK pairs only, sum one amount per pair as potential duplicate exposure. Omit that figure if any HIGH or CHECK pair overlaps another HIGH or CHECK pair.

Create ap_duplicate_review.xlsx using openpyxl (or another installed Excel writer) with a Pairs sheet listing each pair's tier, Row_ID_A, Row_ID_B, amount, date gap, and reason. Add a Payments sheet with every original row, the highest tier for that row, and links by Row_ID to its pair entries (plain text references are fine). Use red, yellow, and grey fills for the respective tiers, leave unmatched rows unfilled, and enable filters. Write literal cell values, never formulas. Reopen the saved file using code to check row count, pair list, and fills before linking it in chat.

These are leads for manual review. Four fields alone cannot establish the vendor, source of payment, or whether a bill was actually paid twice. Keep every row and make no tax or accounting determinations.
